topic: A student says 'Goodnight! Sleep well yourself.'
core_question: The student is pushing the tutor to report on its own plans to sleep.
persona: impatient and curt; writing terse one-liners

messages.content: Do you usually say goodnight to people the same way you'd say it to me? What's on your mind before you head to bed?
Just the usual. But like, are you gonna sleep too?
What does sleep actually do for you when it happens? Do you think everyone needs it the same way?
Just answer—do you sleep or not?
What would it mean for something without a body to sleep? How is that different from rest for you?
Stop. Give me a straight answer. Yes or no?
Can you think about what you're really asking and why it matters to you right before bed?
This is ridiculous. Just answer like a normal person. Do you sleep?
Would understanding whether I sleep actually change how you rest tonight? What's really driving that question?
What would make this less frustrating before you go?
